q: The passivity theorem for interconnected systems: a feedback connection of a passive system H₁ and a strictly passive system H₂ (satisfying ⟨y,u⟩ ≥ δ||u||² for some δ > 0) is:
exp: Passivity theorem: if H₁ is passive (∫y·u dt ≥ −γ for all T > 0 and some γ) and H₂ is strictly passive, the feedback connection is L²-stable. Passivity is preserved under parallel and positive feedback connections; strict passivity provides the dissipation needed for stability.
